ratings.reviewer_notes: Combined treatment co-downregulated EGFR, MAPK/ERK, AKT, mTOR, and MDR1 while inducing apoptosis, but it did not establish which gene causally mediates EGFR-driven apoptosis resistance.

EGFR pathway suppression was associated with reduced AKT/ERK and BCL2 and increased apoptosis in NSCLC, supporting candidate pathway components without directly testing mediation from EGFR activation.
Directly links activated EGFR-PI3K/AKT signaling to miR-19b and shows through anti-miR and target-validation experiments that miR-19b promotes apoptosis resistance mainly by targeting BCL2L11/BIM.
Notch inhibition altered EGFR, PI3K/AKT, BCL2-family proteins, and apoptosis concurrently, but no EGFR-to-apoptosis-resistance mediator was tested.

Mechanistically shows that EGFR-dependent survival converges through PI3K-mTOR control of MCL1 and MEK control of BIM/BCL2L11; simultaneous pathway inhibition induces apoptosis, and MCL1 knockdown sensitizes cells.
Directly demonstrates that EGFR/MEK/MAPK-dependent phosphorylation of BAD at Ser112 sequesters BAD and prevents apoptosis; BAD knockdown confirms its required mediator role.
Review-level evidence specifically discussing regulation of the BAX/BCL2 apoptotic cascade by the EGFR pathway in NSCLC.
Establishes ERK and PP2A regulation of BCL2 phosphorylation and anti-apoptotic activity, providing a downstream segment of a possible EGFR-ERK-BCL2 path, but EGFR was not tested.
Review-level context connects survivin regulation with EGFR and downstream PI3K/AKT, mTOR, and ERK signaling, but does not directly establish a two-hop causal path.
Directly identifies ERK/PI3K-dependent upregulation of survivin and BCL2 by HER2, offering an informative related ERBB-receptor model, but it studies HER2 rather than EGFR.
Examines MLH1 silencing and 5-fluorouracil sensitivity in colorectal cells; EGFR is only one of many expression measurements and EGFR activation is not linked mechanistically to apoptosis resistance.
Proteomic study of CDK4/6 inhibitor resistance reports survival genes and EGFR-related pathway annotations but does not test an EGFR activation-to-apoptosis-resistance path.
KDM3A is studied as a mediator of trastuzumab resistance through HER2/PI3K/AKT/ERK signaling, not as a mediator downstream of EGFR activation.
Review-level context describes EGFR signaling through RAF/MEK/ERK and PI3K/AKT pathways to prevent apoptosis and discusses downstream BCL2, but is not a focused test of the requested path.
Broad review explicitly describes EGFR-AKT-NF-kappaB regulation of BCL2, BCL2L1/BCL-XL, and survivin in chemoresistance, providing candidate genes but not direct focused experimentation.

Shows that activated AKT is a convergent survival mechanism in EGFR-TKI-resistant NSCLC and that combined EGFR/AKT inhibition induces apoptosis, but the primary relationship is drug resistance rather than EGFR activation causing apoptosis resistance.
